classification.difficultyReason: Identify the sine curve and the line with intercept 2 and negative gradient among supplied graph pairs.

content.prompt: Which graph could be used to solve $\sin x=2-x$?

spec.description: Cosine curve and decreasing line; labelled option A.
spec.mathematics: y=cos x and y=2-x; horizontal ticks at 2 and pi; vertical ticks at -2, -1, 1 and 2; no grid.

spec.description: Sine curve and decreasing line; labelled option B.
spec.mathematics: y=sin x and y=2-x; horizontal ticks at 2 and pi; vertical ticks at -2, -1, 1 and 2; no grid.

spec.description: Sine curve and increasing line; labelled option C.
spec.mathematics: y=sin x and y=x-2; horizontal ticks at 2 and pi; vertical ticks at -2, -1, 1 and 2; no grid.

spec.description: Cosine curve and increasing line; labelled option D.
spec.mathematics: y=cos x and y=x-2; horizontal ticks at 2 and pi; vertical ticks at -2, -1, 1 and 2; no grid.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=\sin x$ and $y=2-x$. The sine curve passes through the origin, rises to a maximum and crosses the horizontal axis again at $x=\pi$. The line has gradient $-1$, vertical intercept $2$ and horizontal intercept $2$. These are the two graphs shown in B.

Correct answer: B.
